newsitem.title: USA: Massport board votes to double Tobin tolls to $1.
newsitem.headline: Massport board votes to double Tobin tolls to $1.

text.p: Massachusetts Port Authority Board voted unanimously to double the tolls on the Tobin Bridge on Thursday, marking the first increase in almost half a century, State House News Service reported.

The Tobin, which connects downtown Boston to the North Shore, has cost drivers 50 cents since 1953. But starting at 10 pm on June 30, motorists heading into the city will have to pay $1 to get across.
"This isn't an unanticipated development," board chairman Mark Robinson said before members passed the proposal on a voice vote.
According to Mary Jane O'Meara, director of the bridge, the Tobin's operating and capital costs total about $17 million annually, while revenues account for about $6 million a year.
Doubling the toll will still leave a deficit, Massport needs to trim it.
In the recently passed Metropolitan Highway Systems law, the authority was directed to pay $200 million toward the cost of the $10.7 billion Third Harbor Tunnel/Central Artery project.

The new law will almost surely prompt other toll increases. The Massachusetts Turnpike Authority gained control of the three harbor tunnels in the MHS legislation, and is expected to approve toll hikes to $2 on the Callahan and Sumner Tunnels when it meets June 24. The Ted Williams Tunnel is already $2 and project managers say it will not go up.
The unanimity and brief discussion notwithstanding, the Tobin toll hikes caused a stir in several North Shore communities, most notably Revere.

Rep. William Reinstein (D-Revere) was the lone voice against the proposal and told the board the toll hike affects his constituents "in the pocketbook." The average family in his district will spend $250 to cross the bridge every year.
